That's fair, and I think the practical mitigation is isolation. Don’t run the Podman container under the same user as LiteLLM, keep the API keys readable only by the LiteLLM service account, restrict outbound access, and ideally treat the Strix Halo as a standalone appliance. Closed source is still a legitimate concern, but you also have to look at the rest of the stack. A lot of boutique coding harnesses, plugins, and agent tooling introduce their own supply-chain risk while having direct access to source code, repositories, credentials, and developer environments, which can be a substantially larger attack surface.
